worldcup-1930.summary: The very first tournament, timed to mark the 100th anniversary of the host nation's first constitution.
facts: There was no qualifying; only the 13 nations that accepted invitations took part.
The hosts beat their neighbors 4–2 in the final to claim the first-ever title.

worldcup-1934.summary: The first tournament held in Europe, and the first to use regional qualifying to pick its 16 finalists.
facts: It's the only tournament the reigning champions didn't enter.
In the final, the hosts beat Czechoslovakia 2–1 after extra time.

worldcup-1938.summary: Held a year before World War II broke out, it became the last tournament before the war.
facts: Italy beat Hungary 4–2 in the final to win back-to-back titles.
No World Cup was held for the next 12 years.

worldcup-1950.summary: The tournament that returned after a 12-year break caused by the war.
facts: Instead of a knockout final, a final-round league decided the champion.
The hosts' defeat in the deciding match is remembered as the “Maracanazo,” the tragedy of the Maracanã.

worldcup-1954.summary: The tournament where Hungary, unbeaten in 31 straight official matches, led the final 2–0 before collapsing.
facts: West Germany's 3–2 comeback in that final is known as the “Miracle of Bern.”
South Korea, playing in its first finals, lost 9–0 to Hungary.

worldcup-1958.summary: The tournament where a 17-year-old Pelé made his name by scoring twice in the final.
facts: Brazil beat the hosts 5–2 in the final to win its first title.
It was the first time a team from South America won a tournament held in Europe.

worldcup-1962.summary: A tournament in South America where Brazil won its second title in a row.
facts: When Pelé went down injured, Garrincha carried the team.
A brawl between Chile and Italy went down in history as the “Battle of Santiago.”

worldcup-1966.summary: The tournament where the birthplace of football won its first title, helped by a disputed goal in extra time.
facts: World Cup Willie, a lion, became the tournament's first official mascot.
It's also remembered for North Korea's run to the quarterfinals.

worldcup-1970.summary: The tournament where Brazil's third title let it keep the Jules Rimet Trophy for good.
facts: Matches were broadcast live by satellite, some of them in color for the first time.
Yellow cards and substitutions were used for the first time.

worldcup-1974.summary: The tournament where the Netherlands and its “Total Football” had to settle for second place.
facts: The hosts beat the Netherlands in the final.
The current FIFA World Cup Trophy was awarded for the first time.

worldcup-1978.summary: A South American tournament where the hosts won their first title.
facts: The Netherlands finished runner-up for the second tournament in a row.
Kempes scored twice in the final and finished as top scorer.

worldcup-1982.summary: The first tournament to expand the finals to 24 teams.
facts: Italy beat West Germany 3–1 in the final to win its third title.
Paolo Rossi finished as top scorer with six goals.

worldcup-1986.summary: The tournament where Maradona led Argentina to its second title.
facts: Both the “Hand of God” and the “Goal of the Century” came in the quarterfinal against England.
South Korea returned to the finals for the first time in 32 years.

worldcup-1990.summary: Won by West Germany on the eve of reunification, it was the lowest-scoring tournament ever at 2.21 goals per game.
facts: The final was settled by a single penalty from Brehme.
Cameroon became the first team from Africa to reach the quarterfinals.

worldcup-1994.summary: Held in a country seen as a football backwater, it drew more than 3.5 million spectators.
facts: For the first time, the final went to a penalty shootout, which ended with Baggio's miss.
Brazil won for the first time in 24 years, becoming the first nation to win four titles.

worldcup-1998.summary: The first tournament to expand the finals to 32 teams.
facts: The hosts beat Brazil 3–0 in the final.
Zidane headed in two goals from corner kicks in the final.

worldcup-2002.summary: The first World Cup held in Asia, and the first co-hosted by two countries.
facts: South Korea reached the semifinals under coach Guus Hiddink.
Ronaldo scored twice in the final as Brazil won its fifth title.

worldcup-2006.summary: The tournament remembered for a final that ended with Zidane's headbutt.
facts: The final was decided on penalties after a 1–1 draw.
Italy won its fourth title.

worldcup-2010.summary: The first tournament held on the African continent, with the drone of vuvuzelas filling the stadiums.
facts: Paul the Octopus correctly predicted all seven of Germany's matches as well as the final.
Spain won its first title thanks to Iniesta's goal in extra time of the final.

worldcup-2014.summary: The tournament where the hosts lost 7–1 in the semifinal, a defeat remembered as the “Mineirazo.”
facts: Goal-line technology was used at a World Cup for the first time.
Germany won its first title since reunification and its fourth overall.

worldcup-2018.summary: The first tournament where referees could overturn decisions using video review.
facts: Croatia reached the final for the first time.
South Korea beat Germany 2–0 in the group stage.

worldcup-2022.summary: The first tournament held in the Middle East, kicking off in November to avoid the heat.
facts: The final was decided on penalties after a 3–3 draw.
Messi lifted the trophy for the first time at his fifth World Cup.

worldcup-2026.summary: The first tournament co-hosted by three countries, with the finals expanded to 48 teams.
facts: The number of matches grew from 64 to 104, played across 16 cities.
Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final to win its second title.
